newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Europe wants Turk Cypriots in talks, says official.
newsitem.headline: Europe wants Turk Cypriots in talks, says official.

text.p: A senior European Union official said on Wednesday that the bloc wanted Turkish Cypriots to also take part in talks due to start next year on the accession of Cyprus.

European External Affairs Commissioner Hans Van Den Broek spoke to reporters at the start of a three day visit to the eastern Mediterranean island, which since 1974 has been divided between the Turkish and Greek Cypriot communities.

Greece, and to a lesser extent Cyprus, have reacted angrily to the push by the union this week to include a phrase calling for participation of Turkish Cypriots in a statement on the island's talks to join the EU.

"The line that was disputed said literally that the Council will express the hope that the Turkish Cypriot community could be involved in the accession process as soon as possible," Van Den Broek said on arrival in Cyprus on Wednedsday night.

"I think that still remains very much our common wish. I don't think that is only the wish of the European Union. It exactly means that during this year the process of rapprochement, by coming closer to a political solution, will begin to show results," he said.

Dutch European Affairs Minister Michiel Patijn has said Cyprus' accession to the EU would be politically and almost physically impossible without at least some progress made on reaching a solution between the island's Greek and Turkish communities.

"We all realise that, unless progress is made between the communities, accession is politically and almost physically impossible," Patijn told a news conference in Brussels after the association council on Tuesday.
The island has been divided since Turkey invaded its north in 1974 in response to a Greek Cypriot coup backed by the military ruling Greece at the time.

The Greek Cypriot administration in the south is internationally recognised as the island's only government. The Turkish Cypriots declared their own state in the north in 1983, which is recognised only by Ankara.
Earlier, Greece said its European partners would pay a price for pressing to include Turkish Cypriots in talks on Cyprus' accession and repeated threats to block further EU enlargement.
